title: Chicago Super Coach — choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Public Way. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Public Way
options.lineage: Chicago street blades, the numbered grid, and public-way wayfinding
options.thesis: A charter company is a wayfinding system with wheels — so the site is built as one, not as a highway photo with a quote bar on top.
options.viewport: Full-bleed enamel-green field. A mono grid coordinate rules the top. One oversized white gothic line states the offer. The only proof shown is the two real numbers we own — 57 and 13 — set at display scale. The primary action is a high-vis amber blade, not a button.
options.risk: Green plus high-vis drifts toward municipal DOT or construction yard if the amber spreads past the action. Held by type discipline and keeping amber under 5% of the surface.

options.label: Build Instructions
options.lineage: numbered brick build-instruction booklets on sky-blue pages
options.thesis: The charter assembles in numbered steps, with 1:1 seat call-outs and wordless arrows.
options.case: The only challenger that competes: numbered steps map cleanly onto the quote flow, and an exploded seat map is genuinely on-message. Loses on register — it reads juvenile to exactly the corporate and school-district buyers this brand is for.

options.label: Dispatch Terminal
options.lineage: green-phosphor terminal in a midnight machine room
options.thesis: The booking as a live typed transcript glowing on curved glass.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a monospace transcript hides the fleet and the offer, and the school secretary booking a field trip does not identify with a machine room.

options.label: Datamatics Field
options.lineage: black-and-white data-sublime barcode fields and sine lattices
options.thesis: Schedules and capacities rendered as a strobing barcode lattice.
options.case: Fuses poorly: gallery-grade abstraction with nowhere to put a capacity, a phone number, or a call button. Strobing also fights the accessibility floor this audience needs.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What every charter-bus site ships, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Full-bleed motorcoach on a highway at golden hour, navy-and-gold overlay, a 'Travel in Style' headline, and a three-step quote bar floating over the photo.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the twelve competitors the organizer has open in other tabs — and it needs real fleet photography you do not have yet.
